Controllers as Plain Functions

req and res, no route-model binding, and a flat group of exported functions instead of a class.

A Laravel TicketController is a class, and each action (index, show, store, ...) is a method on it, with the framework instantiating the class and injecting a typed Request for you. This project's controllers are plain exported functions, grouped in one file per resource — no class, no constructor, no dependency injection container. An imported module is already a singleton in Node, which is the idiomatic substitute for what a DI container gives you in Laravel.

Figure 1.7 shows two of the three ticket controller functions (the third, createTicket, follows the same shape and is covered on the next slide):

// Figure 1.7: reading tickets (src/controllers/ticket.controller.js, excerpt)
import * as ticketService from '../services/ticket.service.js';
import asyncHandler from '../middleware/asyncHandler.js';

export const getAllTickets = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const tickets = await ticketService.getAllTickets();
  res.json(tickets);
});

export const getTicketById = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const id = Number(req.params.id);
  const ticket = await ticketService.getTicketById(id);

  if (!ticket) {
    return res.status(404).json({ error: { message: `Ticket ${id} not found` } });
  }

  res.json(ticket);
});

Every controller function takes (req, res) — Express's request and response objects — and reads whatever it needs directly off req: req.params.id for the :id route parameter from ticket.routes.js (previous topic). There's no route-model binding like Laravel's function show(Ticket $ticket) automatically loading a model for you — getTicketById fetches it itself, and handles the not-found case itself, by hand.

Also notice req.params.id is wrapped in Number(...). Express route parameters always arrive as strings, even for a route like /:id that only ever matches digits — so comparing it against a numeric ID without converting first would silently never match. asyncHandler wrapping each function is covered properly later this lesson; for now, read it as "makes async errors in this function reach Express safely."
